To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
5-HT2 receptor activation increases KCC2 expression, thereby increasing GABA- and glycine-mediated inhibition and restoring the alternating pattern of locomotor activity after injury.

(1) 5-HT2 receptor activation can restore the alternating pattern in the adult rat spinal cord after injury and that (2) 5-HT receptor activation can up-regulate K+–Cl− cotransporters, restore inhibition and reduce spasm in a rodent model of spasticity.
5-HT2 receptor activation restores the alternating pattern after spinal injury by increasing the strength of postsyntaptic inhibition through up-regulation of KCC2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of 5-HT in the development and plasticity of the spinal cord, in particular the modulation of the chloride homeostasis and its consequences for the strength of inhibition.
the development of new therapeutic approaches to reduce the consequences of spinal cord injury.
the role of 5-HT, in particular 5HT2A receptors, in the development and maintenance of the alternating pattern and the modulation of the strength of postsyaptic inhibition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

5-HT2 receptor agonists are able to restore the left-right alternance and the reciprocal inhibition between flexor and excitator motoneurons in the adult spinal cord, and that this effect is due to the modulation of the postsynaptic action and strength of inhibitory synapses.

serotonin plays a crucial role in the maturation of locomotor circuits and that its action is mediated, at the level of the spinal cord, through the modulation of postsynaptic GABAergic and glycinergic inhibition.
5-HT2 receptor agonists are effective in reducing spasticity and in restoring the alternating pattern of locomotion in spinal cord injured animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the maturation of the spinal locomotor networks is associated with an increase in the expression of the 5-HT2 receptor and of the KCC2 transporter, both of which are essential for the development of a functional spinal locomotor network.
the serotonergic modulation of the KCC2 expression and the consequent restoration of inhibition is crucial for the development and the functional recovery of spinal locomotion.
5-HT2 receptor activation restores the alternating pattern by increasing the strength of inhibition and the efficacy of commissural interneurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-HT2 receptor agonists could be useful for the treatment of spasticity after spinal cord injury.
5-HT2 receptor agonists may represent a novel therapeutic strategy in the treatment of spasticity and neuropathic pain.
the serotonergic system plays an important role in the maturation and the functional recovery of the spinal locomotor networks.
